doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Radio Deluxe, new artists, and the importance of material
summary: He discusses eighteen years of Radio Deluxe, hearing new artists, and choosing good material. He did not turn to Sinatra until his 40s.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah. I agree. We’ll have to wrap up here so you can get — you have a gig tonight. Do you have anything that you’d like to share about Radio Deluxe, which is very deluxuous. Is that a word?
You can use that in your next song, okay, I give you permission.

That’s pretty good. Well you know we’ve done the show for eighteen years I think. And it’s been a great way to keep up on what everybody’s doing, you know that’s the one thing I really like about it is we — and unfortunately it’s the bane of Spotify in that you can go onto Spotify or actually I go to iTunes and there’s new releases. And I can hear just what the new releases are and find them and try to you know incorporate, you know there is a lot of great new music out there. There’s a lot of great singers, male and female. And great jazz musicians. So it’s fun to, I mean last week’s show there was at least four new singers out there, or jazz musicians like Isaiah and Benny Benack III and Samara Joy and this girl Katie Kortum. And then the funny thing was is I was that person 33 years ago, you know I was making “All of Me” and “Naturally” and all those records that were big deals back — you know that was when it was a big deal to put out your record and all right are we on the charts, what have we done?
Do you have people contacting you like boy I wish you’d play this — play my record?

Sometimes people will say, you know, or you’ll meet somebody and they give you a record or here and there and, or you see it on FaceBook, “I just had new album out” and you go and look at it. The material is the thing. That’s what separates I think the winners from the losers and for lack of a better term is that I’ve heard, I remember there was a young girl made a record and one of the songs was “Second Time Around.” And I was like well the first time around must have been sixth grade, you know? If you’re the “Second time Around” it’s lovelier the second time around so it’s like think about your material. You’re singing “Lush Life” already you know. And I’ve had people have that — not argument but that discussion. You know I didn’t get around to Sinatra ‘til I was in my 40s. I was trying to find this material I could sing, and so finally felt I had a little © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
something to offer that I could find arrangements that would work so that was always a challenge too.
